newsitem.title: USA: NEES invites fewer than 10 to submit bids.
newsitem.headline: NEES invites fewer than 10 to submit bids.

text.p: New England Electric System has asked fewer than 10 bidders for its 18 non-nuclear electric generating plants up for sale to submit formal, binding bids ahead of a mid-July deadline, a spokeswoman said Tuesday.
NEES expects to sign a purchase and sales agreement for the assets at the earliest in August, but more likely in September or later, spokeswoman Jackie Barry said.

Originally, 25 groups, including some multi-national companies, submitted non-binding bids in the first round of the auction. NEES had previously set a second round deadline of June 30, but moved that back to mid-July, Barry said.

The assets, which have a book value of $1.2 billion, consist of 4,000 megawatts of fossil and hydro capacity, including three fossil-fuel plants, a pumped storage hydro plant, and 14 hydroelectric facilities, as well as 1,500 megawatts of purchased power contracts.
NEES Chief Executive John Rowe said last week that he expected the auction to generate "quite intense" competition.

Rowe has estimated the company's stranded assets at $3 billion to $4.5 billion but said that higher figure could come down with a successful sale of the generating assets and increasing demand for electricity.
